question.problem: Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275210/assets/6052e4c3f0ad4e3ddf02b9200c89e808b24a8820de6445677ef0d685927b7b80.svg) is a non-zero vector that is orthogonal to the set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275210/assets/c09dc7dd7a9e4b4493e3c1e2c1324dffe991e8948a371c0ab9d4de9828c280a3.svg) find the value of $\dfrac{a+c}{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
The vector $\mathbf{u}$ is orthogonal to the set $W$ if $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}_1=0$ and $\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{w}_2=0.$ So, we need to solve the following system:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275210/assets/fafbc63ea1e75cd6d7f1dfc93e7e5a83d8f570c6c3a7b356f818debbb091cdfb.svg)

We write the corresponding augmented matrix $M$ and reduce it to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, we have $2$ pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd ones), so $x_3$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we get $x_2=-x_3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we get $x_1=-3x_3.$ So, the general solution is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275210/assets/a9bbd5f866831a70146beb08aa61180fe7dc3aa27e10a767e5fe070de675349e.svg)

Setting $x_3=1,$ we get the vector 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14275210/assets/324a22d18daa5c69f63e89036b6e728a41b8d2eb5a0b13422d733b8625ec1652.svg)

Therefore, we obtain $a=-3,$ $b=-1,$ and $c=1.$

Finally, $\dfrac{a+c}{b}=\dfrac{-3+1}{-1}=2.$
